claim: 75 ± 5% of the myelinated axons were Lhx6-positive in the stratum radiatum at P35
source: We evaluated that 75 ± 5% of the myelinated axons were Lhx6-positive in the stratum radiatum at P35 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, D; Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Quantitative data from immunostaining experiments with reference to figure and source data

claim: 4.1B KO mice displayed a severe loss of myelin sheaths in the hippocampus at P35
source: Strikingly, we observed that 4.1B KO mice displayed a severe loss of myelin sheaths in the hippocampus as shown in Figure 1.
evidence: Direct observation from immunostaining shown in Figure 1

claim: The myelin pattern was selectively altered in the hippocampus of the 4.1B KO mice, markedly in the stratum radiatum both at P35 and P70
source: The myelin pattern was selectively altered in the hippocampus of the 4.1B KO mice, markedly in the stratum radiatum both at P35 (Figure 1B) and P70 (Figure 1F and H, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1H) as an indication that myelination of inhibitory interneurons may be severely affected.
evidence: Observations from multiple time points shown in figures

claim: Only a slight dysmyelination was observed in the molecular layer of the dentate gyrus
source: Only a slight dysmyelination was observed in the molecular layer of the dentate gyrus, which receives numerous excitatory projections from the entorhinal cortex (Figure 1B inset and Figure 3D).
evidence: Observation from immunostaining with anatomical context

claim: No massive loss of myelin was observed outside the hippocampus in the corpus callosum or somato-sensory cortex
source: We did not observe any massive loss of myelin outside the hippocampus, as shown in myelinated tracts like the corpus callosum (Figure 1B) or in the layers of the somato-sensory cortex (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Negative observation from immunostaining in other brain regions

claim: Contactin2-deficiency did not markedly impair myelination in the CA1 hippocampus at P70
source: In contrast, Contactin2-deficiency did not markedly impair myelination in the CA1 hippocampus as illustrated at P70 (Figure 1D).

claim: The total length of myelinated axons and the percentage of Lhx6-positive myelinated axons in the stratum radiatum were similar to control mice in Cntn2-/- mice at P35
source: In Cntn2-/- mice crossed with the Lhx6-tdTomato reporter line, the total length of myelinated axons and the percentage of Lhx6-positive myelinated axons in the stratum radiatum were similar to control mice as quantified at P35 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D; Figure 1—source data 1).

claim: Cntnap2 KO mice show a reduced density of PV-positive interneurons in the hippocampus associated with decreased inhibitory synaptic transmission in CA1 pyramidal neurons
source: As reported in several studies, Cntnap2 KO mice show a reduced density of PV-positive interneurons in the hippocampus associated with decreased inhibitory synaptic transmission in CA1 pyramidal neurons (Paterno et al., 2021; Peñagarikano et al., 2011).

claim: No apparent reduction of myelinated PV inhibitory axons was observed in the hippocampus of Cntnap2 KO mice at P70
source: However, we did not observe any apparent reduction of myelinated PV inhibitory axons in the hippocampus of Cntnap2 KO mice at P70 (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E, F).

claim: The density of paranodes was significantly reduced by 85% in the stratum radiatum of 4.1B-deficient mice at P70
source: The density of paranodes was significantly reduced by 85% (p=0.0060, Student's t test) in the stratum radiatum of 4.1B-deficient mice (n=4 mice/genotype).
evidence: Statistical analysis of quantitative immunostaining data

claim: The density of paranodes tended to decrease in the stratum oriens (–29%) and the stratum pyramidale (–34%) in 4.1B KO mice
source: The density of paranodes tended also to decrease in the stratum oriens (–29%; p=0.1774) and the stratum pyramidale (–34%; p=0.0667).

claim: The density of paranodes was not affected in the alveus nor in the stratum lacunosum-moleculare in 4.1B KO mice
source: The density of paranodes was not affected in the alveus (p=0.8002) nor in the stratum lacunosum-moleculare (p=0.6273) suggesting that myelinated axons connecting extra-hippocampal areas may be preserved.
evidence: Statistical analysis with inference about anatomical implications

claim: Myelination was significantly decreased by 47% in the stratum oriens and by 75% in the stratum radiatum of 4.1B-deficient mice
source: Myelination was significantly decreased by 47% (p=0.0018, Student's t test) in the stratum oriens and by 75% (p=0.0015) in the stratum radiatum of 4.1B-deficient mice, with a 69–90% reduction in the middle region of the layer (bin4: p=0.0004, bin5: p=0.0053, bin6: p=0.0113).

claim: The percentage of Lhx6-positive myelinated axons in the stratum radiatum of 4.1B KO mice appeared similar to control (66.1 ± 3.6% in 4.1B KO versus 75 ± 5% in control)
source: However, we evaluated the percentage of Lhx6-positive myelinated axons in the stratum radiatum of 4.1B KO mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D; Figure 1—source data 1), which appeared similar to control (66.1 ± 3.6% in 4.1B KO versus 75 ± 5% in control) as an indication that dysmyelination was not restricted to Lhx6 GABAergic axons.

claim: The density of PV and SST cells in the stratum oriens and stratum pyramidale of CA1 was similar in the wild-type and 4.1B KO mice
source: We first quantified the density of PV and SST cells in the stratum oriens and stratum pyramidale of CA1, which was similar in the wild-type and 4.1B KO mice (Figure 2A–F).

claim: The 4.1B KO mice did not show a reduced density of PV cells in the stratum pyramidale at P35 in the CA1 region
source: The 4.1B KO mice did not show a reduced density of PV cells in the stratum pyramidale (Figure 2A and B) as quantified at P35 in the CA1 region (Figure 2E; Figure 2—source data 1).

claim: The total length of myelinated PV axons was significantly reduced (–63%) in 4.1B KO mice
source: A high density of PV axons was present in the stratum radiatum of the 4.1B KO mice (Figure 2H) as observed in the wild-type (Figure 2G), albeit they were only partly myelinated in the region bordering the stratum pyramidale (arrow in Figure 2H) and the total length of myelinated PV axons was significantly reduced (–63%, p=0.0317, Mann-Whitney test, n=5 ROIs, 3 mice/genotype) (Figure 2K; Figure 2—source data 1).

claim: The density of SST interneurons in the stratum oriens was preserved in 4.1B KO mice
source: The density of SST interneurons in the stratum oriens was also preserved (Figure 2C, D and F; Figure 2—source data 1).

claim: O-LM axons were only partly myelinated in the lower and upper regions of the stratum radiatum in the 4.1B KO mice with a myelin coverage of 42.3 ± 4.0%
source: However, these O-LM axons were only partly myelinated in the lower and upper regions of the stratum radiatum (arrows in Figure 2J) in the 4.1B KO mice with a myelin coverage of 42.3 ± 4.0% (Figure 2M; Figure 2—source data 1; Video 1) while myelin coverage was 79.7 ± 3.4% for wild-type mice (Figure 2I and M, Video 2).

claim: The total length of myelinated SST axons was significantly reduced (–58%) in the stratum radiatum in 4.1B KO mice
source: The total length of myelinated SST axons was significantly reduced (–58%, p<0.0001, Mann-Whitney test, n=10 ROIs, 3 mice/genotype) in the stratum radiatum (Figure 2L; Figure 2—source data 1).

claim: The density of Olig2-positive cells in the stratum radiatum was 22.3±1.6/105 µm2 in the 4.1B KO mice versus 25.3±2.2/105 µm2 in wild-type animals at P35
source: The density of Olig2-positive cells in the stratum radiatum was 22.3±1.6/105 µm2 in the 4.1B KO mice versus 25.3±2.2/105 µm2 in wild-type animals at P35 (Figure 3E; Figure 3—source data 1).

claim: No decrease in the number of Olig2-positive cells in the CA1 layers was observed that could explain the massive loss of myelin in 4.1B KO mice
source: We did not observe any decrease in the number of Olig2-positive cells in the CA1 layers that could explain the massive loss of myelin in 4.1B KO mice.
evidence: Negative observation from quantitative analysis with inference

claim: No difference in the density of Olig2-positive cells was observed in the hilus, granule cell, or molecular layers of the dentate gyrus in 4.1B KO mice
source: We did not observe any difference in the density of Olig2-positive cells in the hilus, granule cell, or molecular layers of the dentate gyrus (Figure 3F; Figure 3—source data 1).

claim: The developmental loss of myelin induced by the deficiency in the axonal cytoskeletal linker 4.1B may not be associated with change in oligodendrogenesis
source: These results suggest that the developmental loss of myelin induced by the deficiency in the axonal cytoskeletal linker 4.1B may not be associated with change in oligodendrogenesis.

claim: Protein 4.1B mediates interactions between membrane adhesion complexes and the spectrin cytoskeleton and binds Caspr at paranodes
source: Protein 4.1B mediates interactions between membrane adhesion complexes and the spectrin cytoskeleton and binds Caspr at paranodes as schematized in Figure 4A.

claim: 4.1B promotes, via its interaction with Caspr, the growth of oligodendroglial processes and myelin sheath convergence in the developing spinal cord
source: We previously showed that 4.1B promotes, via its interaction with Caspr, the growth of oligodendroglial processes and myelin sheath convergence in the developing spinal cord (Brivio et al., 2017).
evidence: Citation of previous work by authors

claim: Protein 4.1B was detected at the soma of GABAergic PV interneurons and not at the soma of pyramidal neurons in the CA1 pyramidal layer at P70
source: Immunofluorescence staining for 4.1B in the hippocampus indicated that the scaffolding protein was detected at the soma of GABAergic PV interneurons and not at the soma of pyramidal neurons in the CA1 pyramidal layer at P70 (Figure 4D).

claim: Protein 4.1B immunostaining was present in PV and SST axons along the internodes and enriched at paranodes whereas the nodal gap was unlabeled
source: Protein 4.1B immunostaining was present in PV and SST axons along the internodes and enriched at paranodes whereas the nodal gap was unlabeled (Figure 4E and F).

claim: The mean internodal length was significantly reduced in 4.1B KO (34.5±3.1 µm) by comparison with wild-type (43.8±0.3 µm) mice
source: The mean internodal length was significantly reduced in 4.1B KO (34.5±3.1 µm; n=191) by comparison with wild-type (43.8±0.3 µm; n=275) mice (p=0.0286, Mann-Whitney test, n=4 ROIs, 2 mice/genotype).

claim: The maximum internodal length was decreased to 93.8 µm in the 4.1B KO versus 114.5 µm in the wild-type mice
source: The maximum length was similarly decreased to 93.8 µm in the 4.1B KO versus 114.5 µm in the wild-type mice.

claim: The reduction of internodal length strongly indicates that protein 4.1B may be implicated in myelin sheath elongation
source: The reduction of internodal length strongly indicates that protein 4.1B may be implicated in myelin sheath elongation.

claim: At the paranodal junction, the axonal cytoskeleton including 4.1B and ßII-spectrin organizes the boundary between the internodes and the nodal Nav channels
source: At the paranodal junction, the axonal cytoskeleton including 4.1B and ßII-spectrin also organizes the boundary between the internodes and the nodal Nav channels (Figure 4A; Brivio et al., 2017; Buttermore et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2013; Zonta et al., 2008).

claim: The Nav complex is mislocalized distant from the paranodes in the developing spinal cord of the 4.1B KO mice before the convergence of internodes
source: Accordingly, the Nav complex is mislocalized distant from the paranodes in the developing spinal cord of the 4.1B KO mice before the convergence of internodes (Brivio et al., 2017).

claim: In the adult spinal cord, the nodal Nav clusters become properly juxtaposed to the paranodes in mature nodes in 4.1B KO mice
source: In the adult spinal cord, this phenotype is no longer observed and the nodal Nav clusters become properly juxtaposed to the paranodes in mature nodes.

claim: Myelination along Lhx6-positive axons was partly discontinuous in the stratum radiatum at P70
source: As illustrated in Figure 5A, myelination along Lhx6-positive axons was partly discontinuous in the stratum radiatum at P70, leaving uncovered axonal segments (asterisks).

claim: Nav channels were detected at nodes and branch points in hippocampal GABAergic interneurons
source: Nav channels were detected at nodes (Figure 5B, B' and G) and branch points (Figure 5C and C').

claim: Heminodal clustering of Nav channels was observed for interspaced internodes
source: Heminodal clustering of Nav channels was observed for interspaced internodes (Figure 5E).

claim: The lengths of nodal Nav immunostaining measured between two paranodes were higher at P30 than at P70
source: We noticed that the lengths of nodal Nav immunostaining measured between two paranodes were higher at P30 than at P70.

claim: At the age of P30, 44% of the nodes displayed a length >2 µm versus only 22% at P70
source: At the age of P30, 44% of the nodes displayed a length >2 µm versus only 22% at P70, indicating that the internodes may still elongate during the late developmental stage (Figure 5D; Figure 5—source data 1).

claim: A gap was observed between the site of Nav clustering and the paranode at heminodes of 4.1B-deficient inhibitory axons
source: Interestingly, we observed at heminodes of 4.1B-deficient inhibitory axons, a gap between the site of Nav clustering and the paranode stained for Caspr (Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) as compared to control mice (Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).

claim: The gap at heminodes could reach 10 µm and displayed a mean value of 2.25±0.51 µm significantly different from the control value (0.04±0.02 µm)
source: The gap could reach 10 µm and displayed a mean value of 2.25±0.51 µm significantly different from the control value (0.04±0.02 µm; p<0.0001, Mann-Whitney test, n=25 heminodes, 2 mice/genotype; Figure 5I; Figure 5—source data 1).

claim: The length of heminodal Nav clusters was similar in control (1.96±0.29 µm) and in 4.1B KO (1.84±0.12 µm) mice
source: By contrast, the length of heminodal Nav clusters was similar in control (1.96±0.29 µm) and in 4.1B KO (1.84±0.12 µm) mice (p=0.427, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 5J; Figure 5—source data 1).

claim: A gap was observed between nodal Nav and convergent internodes in 4.1B KO mice by comparison with control ones
source: A gap could also be observed between nodal Nav and convergent internodes stained for MBP (Figure 5H) in 4.1B KO mice by comparison with control ones (p=0.0029, Mann-Whitney test, n=26 in 4.1B KO and n=87 in control, 2–3 mice/genotype; Figure 5I; Figure 5—source data 1), together with an increase in the length of nodal Nav clusters (Figure 5J; Figure 5—source data 1).

claim: The mean length of nodal Nav in 4.1B KO (1.92±0.25 µm) was significantly increased by comparison with control mice (1.59±0.14 µm)
source: The mean length of nodal Nav in 4.1B KO (1.92±0.25 µm, n=26) was significantly increased by comparison with control mice (1.59±0.14 µm, n=87; p=0.0068, Mann-Whitney test).

claim: The positioning of Nav clusters is significantly disturbed at the nodes and heminodes of dysmyelinated GABAergic interneurons of 4.1B-deficient hippocampus
source: Thus, the positioning of Nav clusters is significantly disturbed at the nodes and heminodes of dysmyelinated GABAergic interneurons of 4.1B-deficient hippocampus.
evidence: Summary inference from Nav distribution data

claim: Immunostaining for Kv1.2 was detected at the juxtaparanodes or hemi-juxtaparanodes under the compact myelin including at branch points both in Lhx6- and PV-positive axons
source: As expected, immunostaining for Kv1.2 was detected at the juxtaparanodes or hemi-juxtaparanodes under the compact myelin including at branch points both in Lhx6- and PV-positive axons (Figure 6A and B).

claim: Deletion of Cntn2 or Cntnap2 induced a strong decrease in Kv1 channel clustering at the juxtaparanodes of PV myelinated axons in the CA1 hippocampus at P70
source: As analyzed in double-blind experiments, deletion of Cntn2 or Cntnap2 induced a strong decrease in Kv1 channel clustering at the juxtaparanodes of PV myelinated axons in the CA1 hippocampus at P70 (Figure 6D–F), although a residual expression of Kv1 was still present at some juxtaparanodes in both mutants.
evidence: Quantitative immunostaining analysis in double-blind experiments

claim: The percentage of paranodes bordered by Kv1.2 immunostaining in PV axons was significantly reduced by 30% in Cntn2 KO and 53% in Cntnap2 KO mice
source: The percentage of paranodes bordered by Kv1.2 immunostaining in PV axons was significantly reduced by 30% in Cntn2 KO and 53% in Cntnap2 KO mice (p<0.0001, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 6C; Figure 6—source data 1).

claim: The scaffolding protein 4.1B is known to bind Caspr2 and to be required for the proper assembly of the juxtaparanodes both in the PNS and CNS
source: The scaffolding protein 4.1B is known to bind Caspr2 and to be required for the proper assembly of the juxtaparanodes both in the PNS and CNS (Buttermore et al., 2011; Cifuentes-Diaz et al., 2011; Einheber et al., 2013).

claim: A strong decrease (–61%) in the Kv1 clustering at juxtaparanodes of myelinated PV axons was observed in 4.1B KO mice at P70
source: We observed a strong decrease (–61%; p<0.0001, Mann-Whitney test, n=9 ROIs, 3 mice/genotype) in the Kv1 clustering at juxtaparanodes of myelinated PV axons of 4.1B KO mice at P70 (Figure 6C and G; Figure 6—source data 1).

claim: The 4.1B KO mice crossed with the Lhx6-Cre;tdTomato line showed similar decrease in Kv1 clustering at juxtaparanodes in Lhx6-positive axons as compared with control mice
source: The 4.1B KO mice crossed with the Lhx6-Cre;tdTomato line showed similar decrease in Kv1 clustering at juxtaparanodes in Lhx6-positive axons as compared with control mice (Figure 6H, I).

claim: Deficiency in each of the Kv1-associated proteins, Contactin2, Caspr2, and 4.1B induced a pronounced decrease in the juxtaparanodal Kv1 clustering along myelinated GABAergic axons in the hippocampus
source: In summary, deficiency in each of the Kv1-associated proteins, Contactin2, Caspr2, and 4.1B induced a pronounced decrease in the juxtaparanodal Kv1 clustering along myelinated GABAergic axons in the hippocampus.
evidence: Summary of comparative data across mutants

claim: The firing frequencies of fast-spiking PV cells were unchanged in 4.1B KO compared to control mice
source: As shown by the F-I curve during injection of current steps of 100 pA increments, the firing frequencies were unchanged in 4.1B KO compared to control mice (p=0.4128, two-way ANOVA; Figure 7B and C).

claim: The resting membrane potential (Vrest) was not changed in fast-spiking PV cells of 4.1B KO mice (–60.50±1.99 mV in 4.1B KO, vs –57.67±3.26 mV in control)
source: The resting membrane potential (Vrest) (–60.50±1.99 mV in 4.1B KO, vs –57.67±3.26 mV in control, p=0.6748 using Mann-Whitney test) and the input resistance (Rinput) (346.20±37.77 MΩ in 4.1B KO vs 360.11±52.46 MΩ in controls, p=0.8421 using Mann-Whitney test) were not changed (Figure 7D and E).

claim: The input resistance (Rinput) was not changed in fast-spiking PV cells of 4.1B KO mice (346.20±37.77 MΩ in 4.1B KO vs 360.11±52.46 MΩ in controls)
source: The resting membrane potential (Vrest) (–60.50±1.99 mV in 4.1B KO, vs –57.67±3.26 mV in control, p=0.6748 using Mann-Whitney test) and the input resistance (Rinput) (346.20±37.77 MΩ in 4.1B KO vs 360.11±52.46 MΩ in controls, p=0.8421 using Mann-Whitney test) were not changed (Figure 7D and E).

claim: The rheobase and afterhyperpolarization (AHP) area were not significantly affected in fast-spiking PV cells of 4.1B KO mice
source: Similarly, the rheobase (28.80±6.33 pA in 4.1B KO vs 36.67±5.00 pA in controls, p=0.1305, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 7F) and afterhyperpolarization (AHP) area (–276.69±42.71 mV.ms in 4.1B KO vs –185.39±54.05 mV.ms in controls, p=0.2775, Mann-Whitney test) were not significantly affected (Figure 7G).

claim: No significant modification in the intrinsic electrophysiological properties of fast-spiking PV cells was found in 4.1B KO mice
source: Overall, we found no significant modification in the intrinsic electrophysiological properties of fast-spiking PV cells (Table 1; Figure 7—source data 1).

claim: A marked decrease in the mean discharge frequency of 4.1B-deficient Lhx6-positive cells in the stratum oriens was observed
source: We observed a marked decrease in the mean discharge frequency of 4.1B-deficient cells as indicated by the F-I curve depending on injected current steps of 10 pA increments (p<0.0001, two-way ANOVA).

claim: The discharge frequency was significantly decreased upon 100, 110, 120, and 130 pA stimulation in 4.1B-deficient Lhx6-positive cells in the stratum oriens
source: Notably, the discharge frequency was significantly decreased upon 100, 110, 120, and 130 pA stimulation (p=0.0375, p=0.0176, p=0.0022, p=0.014, respectively; two-way ANOVA and Sidack post-test; Figure 7J; Figure 7—source data 2).

claim: The resting membrane potential (Vrest) was unchanged in Lhx6-positive cells in the stratum oriens of 4.1B KO mice (–57.59±1.65 mV in 4.1B KO vs –62. 17±2.93 mV in controls)
source: The resting membrane potential (Vrest) was unchanged (–57.59±1.65 mV in 4.1B KO vs –62. 17±2.93 mV in controls, p=0.2527, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 7K).

claim: Input resistance (Rinput) was significantly decreased by 22% in Lhx6-positive cells in the stratum oriens of 4.1B KO mice (278.94±21.12 MΩ in 4.1B KO vs 357.33±30.30 MΩ in controls)
source: Hyperpolarizing current steps were injected for analyzing input resistance (Rinput) that was significantly decreased by 22% (278.94±21.12 MΩ in 4.1B KO vs 357.33±30.30 MΩ in controls, p=0.0236, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 7L).

claim: The rheobase was not significantly changed in Lhx6-positive cells in the stratum oriens of 4.1B KO mice (52.65±5.79 pA in 4.1B KO vs 38.25±5.73 pA in controls)
source: The rheobase was not significantly changed (52.65±5.79 pA in 4.1B KO vs 38.25±5.73 pA in controls, p=0.1221, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 7M).

claim: The AHP area was significantly increased in Lhx6-positive cells in the stratum oriens of 4.1B KO mice (–526.59±53.50 mV.ms in 4.1B KO vs –351.29±58.99 mV.ms in controls)
source: The intrinsic parameters of APs were also analyzed showing an increased AHP area (–526.59±53.50 mV.ms in 4.1B KO vs –351.29±58.99 mV.ms in controls, p=0.0380, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 7I and N and Table 2; Figure 7—source data 2).

claim: The dysmyelinating phenotype of 4.1B KO mice in SST cells was associated with a selective decrease in their excitability
source: These data indicated that the dysmyelinating phenotype of 4.1B KO mice in SST cells was associated with a selective decrease in their excitability.

claim: 58% of control stratum oriens interneurons had a stationary inflection in the rising phase of the AP
source: Our results showed that 58% of control stratum oriens interneurons (n=12, 9 mice) had a stationary inflection in the rising phase of the AP (Figure 8A2 and C top pie chart).

claim: 65% of 4.1B-deficient interneurons did not display stationary inflection in the rising phase of the AP
source: In contrast, 65% of 4.1B-deficient interneurons (n=17, 8 mice) did not display stationary inflection (Figure 8B2–B and C bottom pie chart).

claim: The difference in the number of cells displaying an inflection point between control and 4.1B KO is statistically significant (p=0.0017)
source: This statistically significant difference (p=0.0017, Fisher's exact test) suggests that the AP was initiated closer to the soma in 4.1B-deficient neurons than in control ones.
evidence: Statistical analysis with inference about AP initiation site

claim: The AIS of SST interneurons in the stratum oriens was significantly shorter in 4.1B KO by comparison with wild-type mice (21.93±0.46 µm in 4.1B KO vs 25.26±0.57 µm in wild-type)
source: We observed that the AIS of SST interneurons in the stratum oriens was significantly shorter (Figure 8D–F; Figure 8—source data 1) in 4.1B KO by comparison with wild-type mice (21.93±0.46 µm in 4.1B KO vs 25.26±0.57 µm in wild-type; p<0.0001, Mann-Whitney test, n=30 interneurons, 3 mice/genotype).
evidence: Statistical analysis of quantitative immunostaining measurements

claim: The AIS onset measured from the soma or the primary dendrite was not modified in 4.1B KO mice (3.8±0.27 µm in 4.1B KO vs 4.13±0.40 µm in wild-type)
source: The AIS onset measured from the soma or the primary dendrite was not modified (3.8±0.27 µm in 4.1B KO vs 4.13±0.40 µm in wild-type; p=0.6509, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 8G; Figure 8—source data 1).
evidence: Statistical analysis of quantitative immunostaining measurements

claim: Dysmyelination in 4.1B KO mice caused a shortening of AIS and a net decrease in the intrinsic excitability of SST cells
source: Taken together, our results indicated that dysmyelination in 4.1B KO mice caused a shortening of AIS and a net decrease in the intrinsic excitability of SST cells.
evidence: Summary inference from AIS and electrophysiology data

claim: A significant increase in sIPSCs peak amplitude was shown in the 4.1B KO mice (45.61±2.93 pA in 4.1B KO vs 31.51±0.88 pA in controls)
source: We showed a significant increase in sIPSCs peak amplitude in the 4.1B KO mice (45.61±2.93 pA in 4.1B KO vs 31.51±0.88 pA in controls; p=0.0022, Mann-Whitney test, n=6 cells from 4 to 5 mice).

claim: The frequency of sIPSCs tended to be increased in 4.1B KO mice (4.97±1.02 Hz in 4.1B KO vs 2.76±1.13 Hz in controls)
source: The frequency of sIPSCs also tended to be increased (4.97±1.02 Hz in 4.1B KO vs 2.76±1.13 Hz in controls, p=0.1320, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 9C; Figure 9—source data 1).

claim: The occurrence probability of small amplitude sIPSCs was decreased in 4.1B KO mice
source: Interestingly, the occurrence probability of small amplitude sIPSCs was decreased in 4.1B KO mice (p<0.0001, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test; Figure 9D; Figure 9—source data 1).

claim: The occurrence probability of sIPSCs with slow rise time was decreased in 4.1B KO by comparison with control mice
source: The cumulative distribution showed that the occurrence probability of sIPSCs with slow rise time was decreased in 4.1B KO by comparison with control mice (p<0.0001, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test; Figure 9E).

claim: Both genotypes showed a significant correlation between the rise time and amplitude of sIPSCs
source: In addition, both genotypes showed a significant correlation between the rise time and amplitude of sIPSCs, as shown in Figure 9F (p=0.0077 in controls and p=0.0072 in 4.1B KO, Pearson correlation test).

claim: There was a significant difference in the elevations of linear regressions between amplitude and rise time of sIPSCs towards a faster rise time in 4.1B KO mice
source: Linear regression analysis of the relationship between amplitude and rise time of sIPSCs showed that while the slopes were comparable between genotypes (Null hypothesis test, p=0.9791), there was a significant difference in their elevations towards a faster rise time in 4.1B KO mice (Null hypothesis test, F=13.55, DFn = 1, DFd = 237, p=0.0003).

claim: Neither the mean amplitude nor the mean frequency of mIPSCs were affected in 4.1B KO mice
source: We found that neither the mean amplitude (28.29±2.33 pA in 4.1B KO mice vs 24.57±2.68 pA in controls; p=0.2224, Mann-Whitney test, n=9 cells from 3 to 5 mice) nor the mean frequency were affected in 4.1B KO mice (2.41±0.47 Hz in 4.1B KO mice vs 2.73±0.51 Hz in controls, p=0.5457, Mann-Whitney test).

claim: The data on mIPSCs indicated that the 4.1B mutation may not modify the inhibitory pre-synaptic terminals connecting pyramidal cells
source: This data on mIPSCs indicated that the 4.1B mutation may not modify the inhibitory pre-synaptic terminals connecting pyramidal cells.

claim: The increased amplitude of sIPSCs in 4.1B KO mice could reflect an enhanced proximal and a reduced distal GABAergic inhibition onto pyramidal cells
source: The increased amplitude of sIPSCs in 4.1B KO mice could reflect an enhanced proximal and a reduced distal GABAergic inhibition onto pyramidal cells.

claim: The distal inhibitory inputs onto pyramidal cells may be reduced as a consequence of the dysmyelination and decreased excitability of SST cells
source: Taken together, these results suggest that the distal inhibitory inputs onto pyramidal cells may be reduced as a consequence of the dysmyelination and decreased excitability of SST cells.
evidence: Summary inference from multiple lines of evidence

claim: Lhx6 is a transcription factor expressed in inhibitory neuron subclasses originating from the medial ganglionic eminence, which includes all hippocampal PV and SST neurons
source: Lhx6 is a transcription factor expressed in inhibitory neuron subclasses originating from the medial ganglionic eminence, which includes all hippocampal PV and SST neurons (Liodis et al., 2007).

claim: A substantial fraction of myelin, both in mouse and human neocortex, belongs to inhibitory neurons by comparison with pyramidal cells
source: Indeed, a substantial fraction of myelin, both in mouse and human neocortex, belongs to inhibitory neurons by comparison with pyramidal cells (Micheva et al., 2016; Stedehouder et al., 2017).

claim: Long-range projecting hippocampal GABAergic neurons are myelinated and play a role in the synchronization among distant brain areas
source: Long-range projecting hippocampal GABAergic neurons are myelinated and play a role in the synchronization among distant brain areas (Jinno et al., 2007; Melzer et al., 2012).

claim: Locally projecting interneurons such as the parvalbumin (PV) cells are frequently myelinated, independently of their morphological subtypes in the mouse hippocampus
source: Surprisingly, locally projecting interneurons such as the parvalbumin (PV) cells are frequently myelinated, independently of their morphological subtypes (i.e. basket, axo-axonic, or bi-stratified) in the mouse hippocampus.

claim: A fraction of somatostatin (SST) interneurons has been reported to be myelinated
source: A fraction of somatostatin (SST) interneurons, which include both long-range and Oriens-Lacunosum Moleculare (O-LM) or bistratified local projecting neurons has been also reported to be myelinated (Micheva et al., 2016; Stedehouder et al., 2017; Stedehouder et al., 2019).

claim: Myelin optimizes action potential (AP) propagation by forming electrical insulation and restricting ion channel distribution
source: Myelin optimizes action potential (AP) propagation by forming electrical insulation and restricting ion channel distribution, but its significance is still elusive in local projecting interneurons.

claim: Oligodendrocytes wrapping of GABAergic axons may be essential for providing axonal metabolic support
source: Oligodendrocytes wrapping of GABAergic axons may be essential for providing axonal metabolic support (Krasnow and Attwell, 2016; Philips and Rothstein, 2017).
evidence: Citation of previous studies with speculation

claim: Myelination of PV interneurons is modulated by neuronal activity or sensory experience and is able to shape the inhibitory circuitry
source: Recent reports indicate that myelination of PV interneurons is modulated by neuronal activity or sensory experience and is able to shape the inhibitory circuitry (Benamer et al., 2020a; Stedehouder et al., 2018; Yang et al., 2020).

claim: GABAergic interneurons present the particularity to be covered by myelin sheaths that display a patchy distribution along the axon
source: In the neocortex and hippocampus, GABAergic interneurons present the particularity to be covered by myelin sheaths that display a patchy distribution along the axon (Benamer et al., 2020b; Micheva et al., 2016; Stedehouder et al., 2017).

claim: The discontinuous myelination of inhibitory ramified axons implies the presence of heminodal structures along mature axons
source: The discontinuous myelination of inhibitory ramified axons implies the presence of heminodal structures along mature axons.

claim: Hippocampal PV and SST neurons display clusters of Na+ channels forming prenodes along the axons before myelination
source: Remarkably, hippocampal PV and SST neurons display clusters of Na+ channels forming prenodes along the axons before myelination (Bonetto et al., 2019; Freeman et al., 2016).

claim: Prenodes can be induced by oligodendrocyte-secreted matrix molecules including Contactin
source: These prenodes can be induced by oligodendrocyte-secreted matrix molecules including Contactin (Dubessy et al., 2019).

claim: Na+ channel clusters along pre-myelinated inhibitory axons are associated with increased conduction velocity
source: Such Na+ channel clusters along pre-myelinated inhibitory axons are associated with increased conduction velocity (Freeman et al., 2015).

claim: The axons of hippocampal PV and SST interneurons are highly enriched before myelination in Kv1 channels that may regulate firing during development
source: We also showed that the axons of hippocampal PV and SST interneurons are highly enriched before myelination in Kv1 channels that may regulate firing during development.

claim: The Kv1 channels are associated with the cell adhesion molecules Contactin2/TAG-1, Caspr2, and ADAM22 and the scaffolding protein 4.1B forming complexes in the juxtaparanodal domains of the nodes of Ranvier after myelination
source: The Kv1 channels are associated with the cell adhesion molecules Contactin2/TAG-1, Caspr2, and ADAM22 and the scaffolding protein 4.1B forming complexes in the juxtaparanodal domains of the nodes of Ranvier after myelination (Bonetto et al., 2019).

claim: Protein 4.1B belongs to a superfamily of proteins that share a conserved FERM domain and serve as membrane cytoskeleton linkers
source: Protein 4.1B belongs to a superfamily of proteins that share a conserved FERM domain (4.1/ezrin/radixin/moesin) and serve as membrane cytoskeleton linkers and participate in a wide variety of cellular events such as motility and cell adhesion (Denisenko-Nehrbass et al., 2003).

claim: In myelinated axons, protein 4.1B is implicated in the organization of the nodes of Ranvier as a linker between paranodal and juxtaparanodal membrane proteins to the actin/spectrin cytoskeleton
source: In myelinated axons, protein 4.1B is implicated in the organization of the nodes of Ranvier as a linker between paranodal and juxtaparanodal membrane proteins to the actin/spectrin cytoskeleton.

claim: At juxtaparanodes, 4.1B is linked to the Caspr2/Contactin2 cell adhesion complex and is required for the clustering of the Kv1 channels as reported in the PNS and CNS
source: At juxtaparanodes, 4.1B is linked to the Caspr2/Contactin2 cell adhesion complex and is required for the clustering of the Kv1 channels as reported in the PNS and CNS (Buttermore et al., 2011; Cifuentes-Diaz et al., 2011; Einheber et al., 2013; Horresh et al., 2010).

claim: At paranodes, 4.1B mediates the linkage between the Caspr/Contactin adhesion complex and ßII-spectrin and participates to the boundary with the nodal complex
source: At paranodes, 4.1B mediates the linkage between the Caspr/Contactin adhesion complex and ßII-spectrin and participates to the boundary with the nodal complex enriched in Nav channels and Neurofascin186 anchored to ßIV-spectrin/AnkyrinG scaffold (Brivio et al., 2017; Zonta et al., 2008).

claim: 4.1B linked with Caspr at paranodes has been reported to promote internodal elongation during development
source: In addition to its role in the organization of ion channel domains at the nodes of Ranvier, 4.1B linked with Caspr at paranodes has been also reported to promote internodal elongation during development (Brivio et al., 2017).

claim: 4.1B-deficiency induces disruption of juxtaparanodal K+ channel clustering and mislocalization of nodal or heminodal Na+ channels
source: We show that 4.1B-deficiency induces disruption of juxtaparanodal K+ channel clustering and mislocalization of nodal or heminodal Na+ channels.
evidence: Summary of findings from the study

claim: 4.1B-deficiency causes loss of myelin in GABAergic axons in the hippocampus
source: Strikingly, 4.1B-deficiency causes loss of myelin in GABAergic axons in the hippocampus.
evidence: Summary of findings from the study

claim: Stratum oriens SST cells display severe axonal dysmyelination and a reduced excitability
source: In particular, stratum oriens SST cells display severe axonal dysmyelination and a reduced excitability.
evidence: Summary of findings from the study

claim: The reduced excitability of SST cells is associated with a decrease in occurrence probability of small amplitude synaptic inhibitory events on pyramidal cells
source: This reduced excitability is associated with a decrease in occurrence probability of small amplitude synaptic inhibitory events on pyramidal cells.
evidence: Summary of findings from the study

claim: Stratum pyramidale fast-spiking PV cells do not appear affected in 4.1B KO mice
source: In contrast, stratum pyramidale fast-spiking PV cells do not appear affected.
evidence: Summary of findings from the study

claim: The results indicate a class-specific effect of dysmyelination on the excitability of hippocampal interneurons associated with a functional alteration of inhibitory drive
source: In conclusion, our results indicate a class-specific effect of dysmyelination on the excitability of hippocampal interneurons associated with a functional alteration of inhibitory drive.
